source.title: Singularity Theorems in General Relativity: Achievements and Open Questions

accepted.question_text: How can singularities in general relativity be assigned mathematical structure and physical properties when singular points, by definition, are not regular points of the spacetime manifold and therefore cannot simply be located as ordinary spacetime events?

evidence.quote: How can one give structure and properties to the singularities?

accepted.question_text: For a general-relativistic spacetime that is extensible, how should one decide whether, how, why, and to what larger spacetime it must be extended, given that extensions may be non-obvious, non-unique, analytically non-unique, or even impossible despite incomplete curves without curvature pathologies?

evidence.quote: what are we supposed to do with given extensible space-times?
the question of singularities is intimately related to the problem of how, why and to where a given extensible space-time must be extended.

accepted.question_text: Can the classical singularity theorems of general relativity be proved under differentiability assumptions weaker than a twice continuously differentiable Lorentzian metric, in particular for metrics whose first derivatives satisfy only a Lipschitz condition, as occurs in matched stellar or galactic spacetimes where matter density jumps at the surface of a body make the metric fail to be C2?

evidence.quote: The theorems are valid if the space-time metric tensor field gμν is of class C2
they have not been proven in general if the first derivatives of gμν satisfy only the Lipshitz condition.

accepted.question_text: How can singularity theorems in general relativity be strengthened or supplemented so that, beyond proving the existence of at least one incomplete causal geodesic, they determine the location in time, severity, and geometric character of the resulting singularity, including whether curvature blows up?

evidence.quote: the theorems do not say anything, in general, about the situation and the character of the singularity.
We cannot know whether it is in the future or past, or whether it will lead to a blow-up of the curvature or not.

accepted.question_text: Do the hypotheses of the singularity theorems leave enough freedom to construct realistic geodesically complete cosmological models that avoid singularities while satisfying well-founded energy and causality conditions, rather than merely producing special non-realistic singularity-free examples?

evidence.quote: there exist well-founded, well-behaved classical models expanding everywhere, satisfying all energy and causality conditions, and singularity-free.
the question arises of whether or not there is room left over by the singularity theorems to construct geodesically complete realistic universes.

accepted.question_text: Can a singularity-theorem-type criterion based on the vanishing of spatial averages of physical variables distinguish singularity-free models that evade existing singularity theorems from genuinely singular models?

evidence.quote: the vanishing of the spatial averages of the physical variables is probably a condition which may allow to distinguish
A conjecture of the singularity-theorem type was put forward in (Senovilla, 1998b) with this purpose.
